claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 variants prepared around 1700 °C have inadequate oxidation performance.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 variants prepared around 1700 °C have inadequate liquid-metal corrosion performance.
Adding a minor amount of Si permits reactive sintering of ZrB2 at approximately 1700 °C.
Si addition enhances mass transport during lower-temperature sintering.
Si addition enhances densification of ZrB2 during sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
Si addition produces an in-situ transient Si-rich phase in the ZrB2 body.
Upon oxidation, the Si-rich phase forms a thin protective SiO2 scale at grain boundaries and the surface.
The resulting SiO2 scale is continuous and adherent.
The SiO2 scale inhibits oxygen ingress.
The SiO2 scale acts as a barrier to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will have higher final density than both high-temperature pure ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will have greater mechanical strength and structural integrity than both high-temperature pure ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than both high-temperature pure ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will have better liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than both high-temperature pure ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free ZrB2.
The protective-scale mechanism is supported by related ceramic systems.
The exact quantitative improvements in oxidation weight gain and corrosion rate are uncertain.
